title: A message from `a` delivered to `b`
request:
`a` ticks twice and sends; the message is delivered to `b`; both are read back

./your_program.sh vector-clock
local a
send a
recv b {"a":2}
get b
get a
note: The receiver's own entry is incremented *after* the merge, and only its own. A receive that increments every entry, or that increments before merging, still looks plausible on one exchange and orders nothing correctly on two.

title: Four comparisons, one per relation
note: The third comparison is the one that catches a map compared by equality: {"a":1} and {"a":1,"b":0} are the same clock written two ways. Compare the union of the names, not the keys of either side.
